skill.name: set-up-woocommerce-google-ads-ltv-bidding
skill.description: Use Product Metrics to set up customer lifetime value bidding for WooCommerce in Google Ads. Check tracking readiness, choose a revenue or profit signal, and verify an eligible test order.
skill.summary: Guide and verify Google Ads bidding based on observed WooCommerce customer lifetime value.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts point to documentation, routine setup checks, or legitimate account configuration rather than shell injection or reconnaissance. The workflow can invoke a local CLI or remote connector, read customer order records, and recommend an unpinned installer. Broader tracking setup and credential handling need clearer authorization boundaries; no evidence of malicious intent or prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Unverified CLI or remote connector selection
remediation.suggestion: Require approval before first use of the connector. Verify the CLI installation and connector identity, then confirm the intended workspace, store, and ad account.
Document a reviewed installer version and immutable skill revision. Keep installation a separate action that the user approves.

remediation.issue: Order checks may retrieve more data than needed
remediation.suggestion: Limit reads to the intended store and the requested test order or sample. Report only verification status and necessary values, without customer identifiers.

remediation.issue: Tracking setup can exceed the requested LTV scope
remediation.suggestion: Keep other ad channels out of the default flow. Explain which data and conversion actions will be enabled, then request approval before importing orders or activating tracking.

remediation.issue: Unrelated credentials may enter agent tool inputs
remediation.suggestion: Remove the credential exceptions from this skill. Direct users to the provider interface for any required authentication and keep raw secrets out of tool calls.
Ship reviewed references with each release or pin their content. Treat fetched documentation as reference material and confirm any new write or grant with the user.

semantic_findings.title: LTV Setup Can Expand Tracking Scope
semantic_findings.description: The LTV workflow falls back to broader tracking setup. The guides include an initial order import, other ad channels, and eight conversion actions without a separate LTV-only scope check. Secondary actions do not change bidding, but they can receive conversion data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback and broader steps are documented. The user still controls account grants and admin actions, so wider sharing is possible rather than automatic.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Exceptions Exceed the WooCommerce Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The secrets rule allows the agent to accept credentials for unrelated integrations and pass them to a command. Raw secrets may enter tool inputs despite the instruction not to log them.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exceptions and command handoff are explicit, while WooCommerce setup says to keep its token out of chat. No evidence found that this workflow actually requests those credentials.

semantic_findings.title: Remote References Can Change After Review
semantic_findings.description: If local references are missing, the skill tells the agent to fetch and follow live Markdown from the publisher. A changed page could introduce steps that were not part of the reviewed revision.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback uses unversioned URLs and specifies no integrity check. The audited package contains the local references, so the fallback is conditional.

content.user_title: Set Up WooCommerce LTV Bidding in Google Ads
content.value_statement: First-order revenue can understate the value of customers who buy again. Use Product Metrics to set up and verify Google Ads bidding signals based on observed WooCommerce order values.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status and identify missing WooCommerce, Google Ads, and Merchant Center connections.
Check a small sample of paid orders to see whether Product Metrics recognizes new and returning customers.
Guide consent configuration and creation of the Revenue LTV and Profit LTV conversion actions as secondary actions.
Explain the cost requirements for Profit LTV and verify whether an eligible test order reached Product Metrics.
Guide the user through choosing one primary conversion action and read back its status after the change.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro, a connected WooCommerce store, and authorized access to Google Ads and Merchant Center.
The user handles WordPress and Google Ads admin steps, including choosing the primary conversion action and setting campaign bidding.
LTV reflects observed orders per connected store, not a forecast. LTV conversions require a recognized customer, matching data, and both analytics and ad user data consent.
Profit LTV requires known order costs. A loss-making order contributes zero to Profit LTV.

use_cases.title: Check Store Readiness
use_cases.description: Identify missing connections or consent settings before using paid WooCommerce orders for value-based bidding.

use_cases.title: Pilot a Value-Based Campaign
use_cases.description: Compare Revenue LTV and Profit LTV, verify the actions, and plan a trial on one Google Ads campaign.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Missing Profit Values
use_cases.description: Check a consented test order and identify whether missing order costs explain why Profit LTV is absent.

prompt_templates.title: Check LTV Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Assess an existing setup without making changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my WooCommerce store is ready for Google Ads LTV bidding. List missing prerequisites and do not change settings.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Test Order
prompt_templates.scenario: Validate tracking before changing a campaign goal.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether Product Metrics received my latest paid test order with consent. Report whether the customer was recognized and which LTV values were available. Omit personal identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Missing Profit LTV
prompt_templates.scenario: Investigate why orders show revenue but no profit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check why my WooCommerce test order shows revenue but no profit value. Identify missing cost settings and tell me what to review without changing them.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Single-Campaign Pilot
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a controlled change to an existing Google Ads campaign.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Revenue LTV and Profit LTV for one campaign. Review consent and cost coverage, then suggest how to choose a target ROAS. List the changes I must make in Google Ads.

output_examples.input: Check whether my WooCommerce store is ready for LTV bidding.
output: WooCommerce, Google Ads, and Merchant Center are connected.
The consent banner is not configured in Product Metrics. Select the banner your store uses, then place a test order with both consent choices allowed.

output_examples.input: Why did my consented test order show revenue but no profit?
output: Product Metrics received the test order and recognized the customer.
The order has a revenue value, but its product cost is missing. Review WooCommerce Core COGS or the configured product cost field before testing Profit LTV.

best_practices: Confirm the intended store and ad account. Verify consent and test order delivery before changing a campaign goal.
Start with one campaign and use only one primary purchase action for that campaign.
Review cost coverage before choosing Profit LTV. Set a target based on the new conversion signal.
anti_patterns: Making both Revenue LTV and Profit LTV primary for the same campaign.
Copying the old purchase action's target ROAS without reviewing the new signal and its coverage.
Pasting the WooCommerce setup token into chat or sharing customer identifiers in a tracking report.

faq.question: What does LTV mean here?
faq.answer: LTV means customer lifetime value. Product Metrics uses observed paid WooCommerce orders, and each eligible conversion carries only what that order adds.

faq.question: What accounts and access do I need?
faq.answer: You need Product Metrics Pro with workspace admin access, a connected WooCommerce store, and Google Ads with Data Manager access and linked Merchant Center.

faq.question: When should I choose Profit LTV?
faq.answer: Choose it when you want to optimize for profit and can supply reliable order costs. Revenue LTV does not need cost data.

faq.question: What consent does Google Ads require for an LTV conversion?
faq.answer: The customer must allow both analytics and ad user data. The order also needs information Google can match, such as an email address.

faq.question: Does setup immediately change how campaigns bid?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics creates secondary conversion actions. You choose the primary action and set the bidding strategy in Google Ads.

faq.question: How does Product Metrics recognize a returning customer?
faq.answer: It uses the WooCommerce account first, then billing email or phone for guest orders. Only statuses marked as paid count.
